title: Non-genotoxic transplantation and in vivo selection through epitope editing.
data_url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10737-8 (supplementary files and Source Data Figs. 1-5, served from static-content.springer.com; licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened every supplementary item that exists: Source Data Fig. 1 (zip with Raw_data_figure_1.xlsx, 108 KB), Source Data Figs. 2-5 (four xlsx, 121-189 KB, 50/27/33/26 sheets each), and Supplementary Tables 1-11 (zip). All are GraphPad-style figure exports with merged multi-row headers; biggest sheets are Fig.2M barcode counts (4x25) and Fig.4K (65x3). The only large table is Supplementary Table 4 (RNA-seq differential expression, 27,080 rows x 8 columns: gene_id, gene_name, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj). Off-target tables: Supplementary Table 6 lists 224 base-editing and 103 prime-editing candidate sites; Tables 7-9 hold 39-185 row result matrices across 3 donors. I searched the whole full text and Europe PMC's text-mined accessions: the only identifiers are two Protein Data Bank structures (4K9E, 6VPC), four clinical trial numbers and a grant number - no GEO, SRA or BioProject deposit for any sequencing data.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The degenerate-codon mutagenesis library over KIT extracellular domain 2 (ECD2, 120 amino acids, NNN codons at each position), its FACS sorting into SR-1-antibody-negative and SR-1-positive fractions, and the amplicon-sequencing analysis pipeline are described only in Methods; I could not open any per-variant table because none is deposited. Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out twice, but the full-text XML gave the complete file list, so nothing is missing from my inventory.

a1_downloadable.note: All nine supplementary items download without login and open cleanly; but the underlying sequencing data (epitope-mapping amplicons, RNA-seq counts, CHANGE-seq) are deposited nowhere - the statement is 'All relevant data are included in the manuscript'.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The only interesting label - per-variant loss of anti-KIT antibody (SR-1) binding from the ECD2 degenerate-codon library - exists solely as a sequence logo image (Fig. 3h) and two validated mutations (D121L, S123P). No variant-level enrichment table in any downloaded file; it would have to be rebuilt from raw reads that were never released.

a3_inputs_present.note: Partly moot: for the off-target tables, genomic coordinates (chr/start/end, hg38) are present and resolvable; for the antibody-escape task there are no variant sequences at all because there is no variant table.

a4_units_stated.note: Source Data sheets are Prism exports with merged headers; values are bare percentages, mean fluorescence intensity and absolute counts with units implied, not in a units column (verified in Source Data Figs. 1-5).

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Largest measurement table I opened is 185 rows (Supplementary Table 9, 'all sites'); mouse groups are n = 4-6; the 27,080-row RNA-seq sheet is a per-gene DESeq2 summary of one stimulated-versus-unstimulated comparison, not 27,080 labelled examples.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~15 MB total across all supplementary files
a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything fits in memory trivially; size was never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Supplementary Table 6 contains 224 base-editing and 103 prime-editing site rows, consistent with the text's '193 and 111 sites' once header and duplicate-guide rows are accounted for; no contradiction found.

a8_label_provenance.note: Where labels exist they are physical measurements (flow cytometry, amplicon read frequencies), not model outputs - but off-target sites were nominated by CHANGE-seq/GUIDE-seq/CRISPOR, so any off-target model would inherit that selection.

existing_models.name: mmCSM-AB / mCSM-AB2 / CSM-AB (graph-based predictors of how a point mutation changes antibody-antigen binding strength)
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report Pearson correlation 0.80 on 242 multiple missense mutations and 0.95 on 101 double/triple mutations, with cross-validation plus two blind tests (figures taken from search-result summaries of the Nucleic Acids Research and Bioinformatics papers, not from a retrieved full text).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not established - I did not retrieve the discussion sections.

existing_models.name: Deep mutational learning (Taft et al., Cell 2022) - machine learning on combinatorial mutagenesis of the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain to predict ACE2 binding and antibody escape
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to predict escape for combinatorial variants; exact numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the natural backbone for an antibody-escape task on the KIT extracellular domain
backbone.hardware: CPU, minutes for a few thousand short sequences
backbone.licence: MIT (ESM-2); the paper's own files are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, non-commercial

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt P10721 (human KIT) plus Protein Data Bank entries 4K9E and 6VPC (KIT extracellular domain bound to Fab-79D and to stem cell factor)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could a model trained on published antibody-escape mutational scans tell you, for any cell-surface therapeutic target, which single substitutions break antibody binding but preserve ligand binding - the design problem epitope editing solves by hand today?

controls.positive_control: A working model must rediscover the paper's own validated hits: H378R for Fab-79D, and D121L/S123P for SR-1.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle escape labels across positions and confirm collapse to the per-position base rate.
controls.external_validation: The 2023 Nature epitope-editing paper on CD123/FLT3/KIT and the CD123 epitope-engineering work in Journal of Experimental Medicine report independently measured escape variants for other targets.

honest_claim_h3: With only a sequence logo and two validated substitutions released, any model built from this paper could claim no more than 'it reproduces two mutations the authors already published', which is not a claim worth making.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence and structure to predict which single amino acid swaps block a therapeutic antibody but keep the receptor working.
plain_idea.train_on: The intended input was each single amino acid substitution in the KIT extracellular domain (KIT is the stem cell receptor CD117), described by sequence context and structure. The number of labelled variants available is effectively zero: no variant-level table was released.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the substitution abolishes binding of a therapeutic anti-KIT antibody while preserving binding of the receptor's natural ligand, stem cell factor. The true answer would come from flow-cytometry sorting of a mutant library followed by amplicon sequencing - measured in this paper but never published as data.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Gene-therapy groups designing 'epitope-edited' blood stem cells currently find these mutations by brute-force library screening for each new antibody; a predictor would cut that to a short list. Even a failed model would say how far structure alone gets you.

more_or_better_data.why: The paper releases no variant-level binding data at all, versus mmCSM-AB's curated antibody-antigen mutation sets of several hundred mutations with measured affinity changes.

confidence_score.why: No replicate-level variant measurements were released, so per-prediction uncertainty could not be calibrated from this paper.

models_beatable.why: mmCSM-AB (2020) is a graph-feature regressor with no pretrained protein backbone and no sequence-identity-clustered split, so it is in principle beatable - but not with data this paper does not provide.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The first condition fails outright: there is no training or test set here to add to anything, and mmCSM-AB's training data is a different assay (measured affinity changes) from this paper's FACS-based binary sorting.

ml_idea: The only ML-shaped question here is: given a cell-surface receptor and a therapeutic antibody, predict which single substitutions abolish antibody binding while preserving ligand binding and signalling. This paper measured exactly that for KIT with a degenerate-codon library, but published the result as a sequence logo plus two validated mutations, so the dataset needed to train or test such a model does not exist in any downloadable form.

effort.compute_note: All files were downloaded and parsed in under a minute on this laptop; size is not a constraint, data content is. No training was attempted because no training table exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the Source Data workbooks and look for a sheet with one row per KIT variant - there is none; the largest measurement sheet is 185 rows, and the mutagenesis-library readout was never deposited.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A5. The interesting label - which KIT mutations escape an anti-KIT antibody - was measured by a degenerate-codon library screen but released only as a sequence logo and two validated hits; I opened all nine supplementary items and found only GraphPad figure exports (largest measurement table 185 rows, mouse groups n = 4-6) plus a 27,080-row differential-expression summary from a single comparison. No sequencing data is deposited in any repository (no GEO, SRA or BioProject anywhere in the text). It is a strong translational biology paper with nothing a model can be trained on.
